rationale:
Keep a bounded module-level cache of labels that already passed check_label. When a str label is seen again, return at once without re-running NFC, hyphen, combiner, per-codepoint and bidi checks. Only successes are cached; failures re-run and raise as before.
Why it should win: check_label runs 24116 times, about 25% cumulative. encode calls it through alabel and decode calls it through ulabel, so each label is validated at least twice, once per direction. Repeated labels across the workload sk

ip the whole per-codepoint loop.
Precondition: Validation is a pure function of the label string. The idnadata tables and the unicodedata version do not change at runtime. Labels are hashable str values.
What the relaxed rule changes: Only labels that previously passed are cached, and validation is deterministic, so a cache hit gives the same None result. Exceptions still arise from uncached labels. Output order is unaffected. Under the lifted rule, the order in which results are produced may ch
ange, for example when work is grouped by label.
title: Memoise per-label validation results across repeated labels in check_label

rationale:
Add a module-level dict mapping a codepoint to its bidi class, filled lazily on first use. check_bidi calls unicodedata.bidirectional once per distinct codepoint and uses the dict lookup afterwards. Optionally build the direction list for the label once and reuse it in the second loop.
Why it should win: check_bidi makes two full passes, each calling unicodedata.bidirectional per character, across 24116 labels. The workload uses only a small set of distinct codepoints across five scripts, so a d

ict hit is cheaper than a C call plus string handling.
Precondition: unicodedata.bidirectional is deterministic for a fixed Python build. Memory growth is bounded by the number of distinct codepoints seen.
What the relaxed rule changes: The same direction values are produced, and error positions and messages are unchanged. Under the lifted ordering rule, labels may be processed in any order, but the cache has no effect on results.
title: Fuse the two bidirectional passes and the PVALID loop in check_label/check_bidi via a per-codepoint class cache

rationale:
Add to the generated idnadata module (produced at build/install time from the existing range tuples) a frozenset of every PVALID codepoint. In check_label, replace the per-codepoint PVALID bisect call with a set membership test; fall back to the existing range logic for CONTEXTJ, CONTEXTO and failure paths so errors are unchanged.
Why it should win: intranges_contain is called 155k times for 24k labels, almost all for the PVALID check in check_label, each doing bisect plus two helper calls. Set

lookup is a single hashed operation. check_label self time plus intranges cumulative are about 10 percent of the profile.
Precondition: The install or build step may generate a larger idnadata table (about 100-150k ints in the set, a few MB of memory, some import time). The set must be generated from the same PVALID ranges and kept in sync.
What the relaxed rule changes: The set holds exactly the codepoints that the PVALID ranges contain, so the branch outcome is identical for every codepoint; e
rror paths still use the original code. Users see a larger installed data module and slightly higher import time and memory.
title: Build-time frozenset of PVALID codepoints for check_label per-codepoint validity test

rationale:
Generate at build time a compact table mapping codepoint to bidi category (or a precomputed flag for RTL-ness), matching the Unicode version that idna targets. In check_bidi, use it to detect RTL labels in a single pass instead of calling unicodedata.bidirectional for each character twice.
Why it should win: check_bidi runs 24k times, calling unicodedata.bidirectional for every character in a first pass, and again in the second pass for RTL labels. Self time is 2.7 percent. Most labels are LTR a

nd only need a quick set check against a precomputed RTL codepoint set.
Precondition: The generated table must come from the same unicodedata version as the runtime; otherwise the unknown-direction behaviour for newer-Unicode codepoints would differ. The install step needs to verify the version match or fall back.
What the relaxed rule changes: The table mirrors unicodedata.bidirectional for all codepoints in the running Python's version, so the results and errors are identical. Users get a gene
rated data file that is tied to the Python Unicode version.
title: Precomputed bidi-class lookup table for check_bidi, built at install time

rationale:
alabel calls the public ulabel on pure-ASCII labels, which lowercases, then runs check_label on the bytes. Add an optional keyword-only parameter or private helper so alabel calls a validation-only path that skips the str/bytes type dispatch, the prefix handling and the decode back to str, whose result is discarded. Keep ulabel's public behaviour as the default.
Why it should win: alabel is 36% cumulative and ulabel 50.7% cumulative; ulabel is invoked for every ASCII label from alabel, and its r

eturned string is discarded. Skipping the wasted work trims per-label overhead across 12058 alabel calls.
Precondition: The new parameter or helper must be additive; ulabel(label_bytes) must still raise the same errors for xn-- labels, including canonical re-encoding checks, and for non-xn labels (check_label).
What the relaxed rule changes: Same exceptions and return values for all inputs; only a new optional internal argument or helper is added. Callers of the public API see no change.
